title: Cyclops: An FSO-based Wireless Link for VR Headsets
authors: Himanshu Gupta; Max Curran; Jon Longtin; Torin Rockwell; Kai Zheng; Mallesham Dasari

problem_statement.en: Narrow-beam optical coupling must simultaneously align transmit and receive mirrors as a headset moves. Receiver angle and position jointly determine optical loss, so endpoint movement demands fast calibrated pointing.
problem_statement.zh: Headset 移動時，narrow-beam optical coupling 需同時對準 transmit、receive mirror。Receiver angle、position 聯合決定 optical loss，endpoint movement 因此需要 fast calibrated pointing。

key_innovation.en: The tracking system supplies headset pose to a learned pointing function that outputs four steering voltages for TX/RX galvo mirrors. Two-stage geometric calibration learns each mirror assembly and their relative coordinate mapping; commodity SFP optics implement 10G and 25G links.
key_innovation.zh: Tracking system 提供 headset pose 至 learned pointing function，輸出 TX/RX galvo mirror 的四組 steering voltage。Two-stage geometric calibration 學習各 mirror assembly 與相對 coordinate mapping；commodity SFP optics 實作10G、25G link。

baselines_compared: Collimated beam, Diverging beam,10G optics,25G optics

key_improvements.en: Measured 10G throughput reaches 9.4Gbps within the tested movement bounds;25G reaches 23.5Gbps. The 25G trace-driven simulation reports 98.6% connected 1ms slots across 500 traces, with per-trace connectivity 95–99.98%. These are short-range terminal and trace-model results.
key_improvements.zh: Measured10G throughput 在 tested movement bound 內達9.4Gbps；25G 達23.5Gbps。25G trace-driven simulation 在500條 trace 的 connected1ms slot 比例為98.6%，各 trace connectivity 為95–99.98%。數字對應 short-range terminal、trace-model result。

evidence: §3–§4 PDFp3–7: joint TX/RX pointing and geometric calibration
§5.4 PDFp11–12:500 user traces and98.6% connectivity simulation
